messages.content: The conference housing desk says the official hotel cannot honor Monday night, despite the confirmation from our last conversation. Please recheck the stay before we rely on it.

You are right to flag it. DC7H42 shows as an incomplete request rather than a valid four-night reservation. The official hotel has rooms Tuesday through Friday only. I’ll compare a split stay with the two four-night alternatives and keep the full trip within the previously approved $2,904.24.

Include taxes, cancellation cutoffs, how I would get to the meeting each morning, and whether either hotel can hold my bag early Monday. My presentation is Tuesday morning, so moving that day is a real drawback.

Here are the tax-inclusive lodging totals for March 1-5. The split stay is $1,253.04: Monday at the Capitol Business Hotel for $247.86, then the official hotel Tuesday-Friday for $1,005.18. Capitol Business is an 8-minute walk from the conference hotel and will hold luggage after 7:00 a.m., but you would need to check out and move the bag before Tuesday’s presentation. The Monday room cancels without charge until 6:00 p.m. Eastern on February 27; the conference block cancels until 6:00 p.m. Eastern on February 26.
What are the two continuous-stay choices?

Capitol Business has all four nights for $1,238.40 including tax. It is an 8-minute walk to the conference hotel, offers luggage storage at any hour on arrival day, and is refundable until 6:00 p.m. Eastern on February 27. The Metro Center Hotel is $876.52 including tax, refundable until 4:00 p.m. Eastern on February 26. From there, allow about 22 minutes each morning: a 4-minute walk, one Metro stop, and roughly 9 minutes on foot at the conference end. Its desk will store luggage from 6:00 a.m. Monday.
So the split is actually more expensive than staying all four nights at Capitol Business?
Yes. The split costs $14.64 more, and it adds a Tuesday checkout and luggage move. Capitol Business for all four nights is both less expensive and operationally simpler.
Show the full trip totals for Capitol Business and Metro Center. Keep the ticketed flights and the same taxi allowance.

With the $1,444.00 ticketed airfare and $120 estimated round-trip taxi allowance, Capitol Business brings the projected trip total to $2,802.40. Metro Center brings it to $2,440.52. Both are below the approved $2,904.24; Capitol Business leaves $101.84 of headroom, while Metro Center leaves $463.72.
How much presentation-day disruption does Capitol Business create? I need to be in the conference room by 7:30 Tuesday.

It avoids the main disruption because you keep the same room Monday through Friday. For Tuesday, leave Capitol Business around 7:12 a.m.; the walk is estimated at 8 minutes, leaving about 10 minutes to reach the conference room. There is no checkout, luggage handoff, or Metro dependency that morning.
And Monday night, with the flight landing at DCA at 9:08?

The existing taxi plan should put you at Capitol Business around 9:45-10:00 p.m. Its front desk is staffed overnight, so late arrival is accepted. Early luggage storage is available but should not be necessary given the evening arrival.
Reserve Capitol Business for all four nights. Do not keep any Tuesday-Friday room at the official hotel, and make sure the failed request cannot generate a charge.

Reserved Capitol Business for March 1-5 at $1,238.40 including tax. Confirmation: CB6K91. Cancellation is permitted without charge until 6:00 p.m. Eastern on February 27; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. The incomplete official-hotel request DC7H42 has been closed with a zero balance and no active room attached. Your flights remain under W4N8JP, and the revised projected trip total is $2,802.40 including the $120 taxi allowance. For Tuesday’s presentation, plan to leave the hotel at 7:12 a.m. for the 8-minute walk.
